newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Wills says no local Liggett impact.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Wills says no local Liggett impact.

text.p: Australian cigarette maker W.D & H.O. Wills Holdings Ltd, which has 28.6 percent of the local market, said on Friday that the Liggett decision in the United States had no local implications.

"There have been widespread reports today in the Australian media of developments affecting the industry in the United States. In contrast to the claims of some anti-smoking activists, these developments have no relevance to Australia," Willis corporate affairs head Suzanne Povey said.
Shares in Wills and fellow local maker Rothmans Holdings Ltd fell sharply in local trade on Friday.
Wills shares ended 19 cents lower at A$2.11. The company is 67 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc.
Rothmans was the hardest hit, with its shares dropping 66 cents to A$8.30.
Rothmans is about 50 percent owned by Rothmans Internatinal Ltd, a 60 percent subsidiary of Swiss-based Richemont AG, The remainder is held by Rembrandt Group Ltd of South Africa.

The Liggett cigarette company said in the U.S. on Thursday that it would settle litigation with 22 U.S. states by paying one quarter of its pre-tax profits for the next 25 years to settle claims and hand over potentially damning documents.
The company also said in its surprise statement that it would admit to the health hazards of smoking, including addiction.
